source.name: Hagerty Valuation Tools (1951 Chevrolet Styleline Deluxe)
source.says: Config list: Deluxe '2dr Bel Air Coupe' 6-cyl. 216.5cid/92hp 1bbl. Also Old Cars Weekly (1949-52 Chevys article): 1951 manual-transmission Chevrolets 216.5-cid, 92 hp at 3,400 rpm.

source.name: Old Cars Weekly - '1949-52 Chevys are gaining in collectibility'
source.says: 1951: 'The hydraulic-lifter 235.5-cid version used in Powerglide-equipped cars ... delivered 105 hp at 3,600 rpm.' (line-wide statement for 1951 Chevrolets; article covers the Bel Air hardtop)

source.name: Hagerty Valuation Tools (1952 Chevrolet Styleline Deluxe)
source.says: Config list: Deluxe '2dr Bel Air Coupe' 6-cyl. 216.5cid/92hp 1bbl.

not_found: Searched Old Cars Weekly, Mac's Motor City Garage (1952 videos, Powerglide history - 1950 only), Curbside Classic (1950 Bel Air article only), Hagerty (1952 Styleline lists only 216.5/92), HowStuffWorks/Consumer Guide, Hemmings. Only Wikipedia (already counted) states 1952 235/105.

source.name: Hagerty Valuation Tools (1953 Chevrolet Bel Air)
source.says: Only config listed: 6-cyl. 235cid/108hp 1bbl. Also Collector Car Market Review profile (VMR): 3-speed/overdrive cars 235.5 ci, 7:1 CR, 108 hp.

source.name: Collector Car Market Review (VMR International) - 1953-54 Chevrolet profile
source.says: 1953 Powerglide cars: compression raised to 7.5:1, 'which bumped the horsepower up to 115'. Mac's Motor City Garage 'Chevrolet Class of 1953' agrees: Blue Flame 115 hp standard with Powerglide.

source.name: Old Cars Weekly - Car of the Week: 1954 Chevrolet Bel Air
source.says: 'The 235-cid power plant produced 115 hp in stick shift cars and 125 with the Powerglide.' Hagerty 1954 Bel Air also lists 6-cyl. 235cid/115hp.

source.name: Old Cars Weekly - Car of the Week: 1954 Chevrolet Bel Air
source.says: 'The 235-cid power plant produced 115 hp in stick shift cars and 125 with the Powerglide.' Collector Car Market Review agrees (Powerglide models 125 hp).
